findings.source_quote: τοῖς δὲ προτέροις οὐκ ἔστι; παρά τι γὰρ αἱ αὐταὶ αἱ πράξεις αὐτῶν εἰσί.
findings.english_quote: “Former ones” and “the same” follow the printed conjectures compared with the versions. The reported Athos readings differ grammatically; “the same” replaces a reported phrase meaning “according to these.”
findings.issue: Footnote b misrepresents the supplied apparatus report. The reported alternative to αἱ αὐταί is καὶ αὗται, meaning “and these,” not “according to these.” The other reported difference, πρώτοις versus προτέροις, is “first” versus “former,” not merely a grammatical difference. These inaccuracies obscure the actual alternatives while the main text correctly follows the selected working readings.
findings.suggested_revision: Correct the note to identify the reported Athos readings as πρώτοις (“first ones”) and καὶ αὗται (“and these”). Explain that the printed edition instead adopts the version-compared conjectures προτέροις (“former ones”) and αἱ αὐταί (“the same”). Do not invent a fluent reconstruction of the reported alternative clause without further evidence. Retain the selected main-text readings; any revised note requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: τοῖς δὲ προτέροις οὐκ ἔστι; παρά τι γὰρ αἱ αὐταὶ αἱ πράξεις αὐτῶν εἰσί.
findings.english_quote: “The first group” and “the same” follow the printed conjectures compared with the versions. The reported Athos readings differ grammatically; “the same” replaces a reported phrase meaning “according to these.”
findings.issue: Independently checked against the selected Greek and supplied apparatus, footnote b gives an incorrect meaning for the reported καὶ αὗται: it means “and these,” not “according to these.” It also characterizes πρώτοις versus προτέροις as a grammatical difference rather than the wording distinction “first” versus “former.” The simplified main text’s contextual reference to “the first group” is compatible with the selected source, but the note does not accurately disclose the reported readings.
findings.suggested_revision: State that the selected Greek uses the conjectures προτέροις (“former ones,” rendered contextually here as “the first group”) and αἱ αὐταί (“the same”), whereas the apparatus reports Athos πρώτοις (“first ones”) and καὶ αὗται (“and these”). Remove “according to these” and avoid supplying an unsupported reconstruction of the alternative clause. Submit the revised note for fresh review.

summary: Both editions cover the selected source’s clauses and preserve its severe denial of repentance, conditional availability of repentance, death consequences, continuing penalty, and speaker distinctions. Both use policy-compatible “servants” and contextual “repentance.” The disclosed working reading “bare” and bracketed “according to” need not be replaced. Revision is required because footnote b inaccurately describes the supplied apparatus alternatives. This review evaluates the supplied working text and attributed reports, not unseen manuscripts or exhaustive collation.
